description: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework

summary.one_liner: TradingAgents is a Python multi-agent framework that uses LLM-driven analyst, researcher, trader and risk roles to analyze a stock ticker on a given date and produce a trading decision, intended for research.
summary.what_it_does: It runs a team of LLM agents modeled on a trading firm: analysts (fundamentals, sentiment, news, technical) work in parallel, then bullish and bearish researchers debate, a trader proposes a transaction, and risk managers and a portfolio manager approve or reject it. A run is started per ticker and date, via a CLI or Python API (TradingAgentsGraph.propagate), and returns a decision. Reports can be saved, including a single HTML page. The framework also includes a backtest over a grid of tickers and dates scored by alpha against a regional benchmark, a persistent decision memory log that settles past decisions, and opt-in checkpoint resume. It supports many LLM providers and Yahoo Finance-covered markets, and uses SEC EDGAR for US fundamentals as filed. The README says it is for research and not financial advice.
use_cases: analyze a stock ticker on a past date
generate analyst-style reports on equities or crypto
run scheduled LLM stock analysis from scripts
study agent debate for investment strategy
how_to_run: conda create -n tradingagents python=3.13 && conda activate tradingagents (or uv venv --python 3.13)
export OPENAI_API_KEY=... (or another provider key), then run: tradingagents
Or with Docker: cp .env.example .env && docker compose run --rm tradingagents
stack: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Mistral, Kimi, Groq, NVIDIA NIM, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI APIs
notable: Mirrors a trading firm with separate analyst, researcher, trader, risk and portfolio manager agents that debate before deciding
Point-in-time data handling: SEC EDGAR filings read as they stood on the run date, to limit look-ahead bias
Built-in backtest over ticker and date grids, scored on alpha versus a regional benchmark
Persistent memory log: past decisions are settled later and fed back to the portfolio manager
Supports many LLM providers, including a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription login and local Ollama or OpenAI-compatible servers, with different models per tier
caveats: Explicitly for research; the README says it is not financial, investment, or trading advice and results may vary widely
Outputs depend on the LLM, temperature and live data, so runs are not reproducible; reasoning models largely ignore temperature
Requires API keys or a paid LLM plan, or local model setup; some data sources (Yahoo statements for past dates, insider trades) are withheld for historical runs
Non-US fundamentals are not from SEC EDGAR and are limited for past dates
